items.title: Burkina/Médias : « Faire de chaque publication un levier de paix et de cohésion sociale », l'appel du président du CSC, Louis Modeste Ouédraogo
items.description: Le président du CSC, Louis Modeste Ouédraogo, rappelle que dans un contexte national marqué par des défis sécuritaires et une circulation accélérée de l'information, journalistes et producteurs de contenus numériques ont une responsabilité majeure dans la préservation de la paix. Leur rôle, insiste-t-il, est également crucial pour la cohésion sociale mais aussi la confiance entre les citoyens et les institutions. En procédant à la clôture des travaux, le président du CSC a d'abord félicité les journalistes et web-activistes pour leur implication tout au long de la session. Il a salué la qualité des échanges, des contributions et des débats qui, selon lui, traduisent l'intérêt accordé aux différentes thématiques abordées. Durant trois jours, les participants ont confronté leurs expériences de terrain, approfondi leurs connaissances et renforcé leurs compétences sur les principes, les méthodes et les exigences de la gestion de l'information en période de crise. Pour le président du CSC, Louis Modeste Ouédraogo, la richesse des discussions témoigne d'une volonté commune de promouvoir une information professionnelle, responsable et utile aux citoyens Le président du CSC a également rendu hommage aux formateurs et facilitateurs pour la qualité de leurs communications, qui ont permis d'apporter des réponses concrètes aux préoccupations exprimées par les participants. Il a aussi salué l'esprit d'ouverture et de dialogue qui a prévalu tout au long de cette rencontre. Lire aussi : Information en période de crise : Le CSC renforce les capacités des journalistes et web-activistes pour une gestion responsable Transformer les acquis en bonnes pratiques Au-delà des connaissances acquises, le président du CSC a insisté sur la nécessité de les traduire en actions concrètes. Selon lui, la véritable portée de cette formation se mesurera à travers les pratiques professionnelles des participants une fois de retour dans leurs rédactions, leurs médias ou sur leurs plateformes numériques. « Les connaissances acquises au cours de cet atelier n'auront de véritable valeur que si elles trouvent une traduction dans vos pratiques quotidiennes », a-t-il affirmé. Dans un environnement marqué par les crises sécuritaires et les manipulations informationnelles, il a rappelé que la qualité de l'information demeure un facteur essentiel de résilience nationale, de cohésion sociale et de renforcement de la confiance entre les citoyens et les institutions. Le rapport général des travaux a été présenté par Mariama Tamboura, journaliste à la Télévision nationale, qui est revenue sur les principaux temps forts et les enseignements de ces trois jours de formation Une responsabilité partagée entre journalistes et web-activistes S'adressant aux journalistes, Louis Modeste Ouédraogo les a exhortés à demeurer les garants d'une information rigoureuse, fondée sur le recoupement des sources, le respect de l'éthique professionnelle et une prise en compte permanente du contexte de crise. Il a également appelé les web-activistes et les éditeurs de contenus numériques à mesurer pleinement l'influence qu'ils exercent sur leurs communautés. Si les réseaux sociaux offrent des possibilités inédites d'informer, de sensibiliser et de mobiliser, cette capacité d'influence doit selon lui s'exercer avec responsabilité, dans le respect des lois nationales et des valeurs du vivre-ensemble. Pour le président du CSC, cette influence doit avant tout être mise au service de la paix, de la cohésion sociale, du développement et, plus largement, de l'intérêt général. Le président du CSC a réaffirmé la conviction de son institution que les médias professionnels comme les plateformes numériques doivent demeurer des espaces de diffusion d'informations crédibles, équilibrées et apaisées. La web-activiste Yasminatou Bidiga a pris la parole au nom de l'ensemble des participants pour exprimer leur gratitude envers le CSC, le PNUD ainsi que tous les acteurs ayant contribué à la réussite de cette session de formation Dans les périodes de crise, a-t-il souligné, chaque mot, chaque image et chaque publication peuvent produire des effets considérables sur les populations. D'où la nécessité pour tous les acteurs de l'information d'agir avec discernement, responsabilité et professionnalisme afin d'éviter la propagation de rumeurs, de fausses informations ou de contenus susceptibles d'exacerber les tensions. Le CSC réaffirme son engagement Profitant de cette cérémonie de clôture, Louis Modeste Ouédraogo a renouvelé l'engagement du Conseil supérieur de la communication à poursuivre les actions de renforcement des capacités des professionnels des médias et des acteurs de la communication. Avec l'appui de ses partenaires, le régulateur entend multiplier les cadres de dialogue, de formation et d'échanges afin d'accompagner l'évolution des pratiques médiatiques et de répondre aux défis croissants liés à la gestion de l'espace civique numérique. Le journaliste Hamidou Kafando a procédé à la lecture des recommandations de l'atelier, mettant en lumière les engagements et les pistes d'amélioration retenus par les participants pour une gestion plus responsable de l'information en période de crise Le président du CSC a par ailleurs exprimé sa reconnaissance au Programme des Nations Unies pour le développement (PNUD), dont l'accompagnement a permis la tenue de cet atelier. Il a également remercié les autorités administratives de la région du Nando, en particulier le gouverneur, pour leur disponibilité et leur soutien, ainsi que l'ensemble des équipes techniques et administratives qui ont contribué à la réussite de la rencontre. Lire aussi : Burkina Faso/Médias : Face à l'intelligence artificielle, Dr Cyriaque Paré appelle à une nouvelle culture de la vérification de l'information En refermant officiellement les travaux, Louis Modeste Ouédraogo a formulé le vœu que les liens créés durant ces trois jours de formation se consolident et que chaque participant reparte de Koudougou avec la ferme volonté de mettre les acquis de cette session au service d'une communication plus responsable. Au-delà d'une simple cérémonie de clôture, son message a résonné comme un appel à faire de chaque journaliste et de chaque web-activiste un acteur de la résilience nationale, conscient que, dans un contexte de crise, l'information n'est pas seulement un droit : elle est aussi une responsabilité dont dépend, en partie, la préservation de la paix, de la cohésion sociale et du développement du Burkina Faso. Hamed Nanéma Lefaso.net

items.title: Trump says 'Board of Peace' reaches Gaza disarmament deal
items.description: July 30 (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday his so-called "Board of Peace" reached an agreement for the complete disarmament of Palestinian Hamas militants and other armed groups in Gaza. In a post on Truth Social, Trump cast it as a "major milestone in the implementation of the Trump 20-Point Plan" to end Israel's war in Gaza. Trump said the deal would be carried out in phases, with Israeli forces withdrawing as disarmament proceeds and an International Stabilization Force working with a new Palestinian police force to secure the enclave.

items.title: Zelensky Asked Trump for a Favor From Elon Musk
items.description: D uring closed-door talks at the White House on Tuesday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky laid out a plan for his country to survive another winter of war with Russia. For it to work, President Trump would need to call in a big favor from his ally Elon Musk. But according to two officials familiar with the conversation, Trump was noncommittal, leaving the future of the plan in doubt. The new proposal, which has not been previously reported, offered the United States a way around sending Ukraine advanced air-defense missiles, known as Patriot interceptors, which the war in Iran has dramatically depleted. Instead, Ukraine would expand its use of another American technology: the Starlink satellite-communications network, which Musk controls. Zelensky asked Trump to secure Musk’s permission for the use of Starlink to guide drone strikes inside Russia, according to the two officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal deliberations. (A third official confirmed Zelensky’s request.) Up to now, Musk has allowed the Ukrainians to use Starlink only on their own territory, including in Crimea and other regions that Russia has occupied. Musk’s aerospace company, SpaceX, has restricted the use of Starlink inside Russia. Ukraine’s campaign of long-range drone strikes has therefore employed less reliable targeting methods, including onboard computers with AI-powered navigation tools. These weapons have been effective at hitting large infrastructure sites in Russia, such as oil refineries and warehouses. But, in his talks with Trump on Tuesday, Zelensky explained the need to hit much smaller and more mobile targets, especially the ballistic-missile batteries that Russian forces have used to hit cities across Ukraine. Last night, as Zelensky and his entourage traveled home through Poland, Russia launched more than 70 missiles, killing at least 10 people in one of the biggest salvos of the war. One of the rockets exploded in Poland. Starlink offers the most precise means available to steer Ukrainian drones to the Russian missile launchers, many of which are mounted on trucks dispersed across Russia. During his visit to the U.S. this week, Zelensky asked to meet with Musk to talk about his plan for targeting these launchers, but the billionaire declined the invitation, according to one person involved in the discussions. Musk and SpaceX did not respond to requests for comment. When they met at the White House, Trump told his Ukrainian counterpart that he would consider the requests, but he did not indicate whether he would eventually grant them, one official told told us. Trump did tell Zelensky that he would talk with Musk about it but did not offer a timetable for that conversation or for his eventual decision. Trump has made no secret of his desire to bring the Russia-Ukraine conflict to a close, and has been frustrated at how long it has taken. One of the officials told us that his eventual decision on Zelensky’s proposal would likely be largely based on whether he felt it could help hasten the end of the conflict. If he thinks that using Starlink would enable Ukraine to push Russian President Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table, then Trump may support it. But if he feels it would only escalate matters, then he likely would not, one official told us. [ Read: Zelensky makes his pitch to Trump ] Trump, of course, has been highly deferential to Putin for more than a decade now, and that has hardly changed during this war. Although he has flashed his frustration with the Russian leader at times, he has mostly stayed skeptical of Ukraine’s cause and its chances. But, one official told us, Trump has been impressed with Ukraine’s recent ability to strike deep within Russia with its drone technology and has sensed that Kyiv has some momentum in the conflict (Trump loves to be associated with winners). The meeting remained convivial and Zelensky invoked the memory of the late Senator Lindsey Graham when making his pitch. W ith the war in its fifth year, Zelensky emphasized to Trump that Ukraine needs to counter the missile threat before the onset of winter, when Russia may again try to use these weapons to knock out Ukraine’s power grid and heating systems, according to the two officials familiar with the talks. Without the ability to hit launchers inside Russia, “we have no clear path through this winter,” one of the officials told us. Last winter, Ukraine still had a limited supply of Patriot interceptors to shoot down Russian missiles and protect its most crucial infrastructure. But the war in Iran has since depleted roughly two-thirds of the U.S. stockpile of these interceptors, according to an analysis published this week by the Center for Strategic and International Studies, a research institute based in Washington, D.C. The CSIS report estimated that the U.S. now has as few as 759 of the most advanced Patriot rockets. Zelensky asked the U.S. to send 300 of these for Ukraine to use this winter. Trump has demurred. Instead, during his talks with Zelensky earlier this month in Ankara, he promised to give Ukraine a license to make its own Patriot interceptors—though Ukraine would not be able to produce them at scale for years. In the Tuesday meeting, Zelensky argued that Starlink could offer a faster and cheaper answer to the ballistic-missile threat from Russia, according to two of the officials familiar with the conversation. Ukraine already has the long-range drones needed to target missile launchers inside Russia. The Ukrainian company that produces many of them, Fire Point, uses various guidance systems to get around the ban on deploying Starlink inside Russia. [ Read: Ukraine’s Dr. Strangelove ] One of the company’s co-founders, Denys Shtilerman, told us that drones equipped with Starlink could prove far more effective than Patriot interceptors in neutralizing the Russian ballistic-missile threat. “Instead of shooting down the arrows, we would strike the archers,” he said. Inside its own territory, Ukraine has already used Starlink-enabled drones to create what it calls a “kill zone” along the front line—a no-man’s-land, dozens of miles wide, where drones can target any Russian forces that seek to advance. With permission to do the same thing inside Russian territory, “we could widen the kill zone to 500 kilometers,” Shtilerman told us. “If they increase the range of their strikes, we would widen the kill zone all the way to Siberia if needed. The technology would allow us to do that.” M usk has long resisted the use of Starlink in warfare. The system depends on the world’s largest constellation of satellites to provide a high-speed internet connection to anyone with a Starlink subscription and a receiver. At the start of the Russian invasion, in 2022, Musk provided Ukraine with Starlink receivers free of charge. Ukrainian hospitals, emergency workers, and government agencies used them to stay online despite Russian attacks on the country’s internet infrastructure. The armed forces of Ukraine soon began using Starlink to coordinate troop movements and pilot drones, and the system became the backbone of Ukraine’s military communications. During some of Ukraine’s most brazen strikes against Russian forces, Musk got cold feet. “How am I in this war?” Walter Isaacson quoted him as asking in his 2023 biography. “Starlink was not meant to be involved in wars. It was so people can watch Netflix and chill and get online for school and do good, peaceful things, not drone strikes.” That year, the Pentagon began contracting with SpaceX for the communications services it provides to Ukraine’s armed forces. The company also created a separate network, known as Starshield, for use in defense and national security. During his talks with Trump on Tuesday, Zelensky suggested that if Musk refuses to allow the use of Starlink for strikes on Russia, the Pentagon could give Ukraine access to the Starshield network for the same purpose, two of the officials told us. One of them added, however, that Starshield would not work as well for Ukraine. “It’s more expensive, more complicated, more difficult to integrate into our systems,” the official said. “We have long figured out how to fly drones on Starlink. It would not be hard for us to send them across the border. But Starshield is a somewhat different system. We would need to figure out how to integrate it.” That leaves Starlink as the cheapest and most reliable guidance system available for Ukraine’s long-range drones. From Musk’s earlier decisions, it can be hard to discern a coherent strategy toward the war in Ukraine. He has used Starlink in ways that each of the warring sides has perceived as helping the other. A few months into the Russian invasion, Musk began to complain about the spiraling cost of providing Ukraine with Starlink service. He refused a Ukrainian request in September 2022 to use Starlink in an attack on Russian warships in Crimea, arguing that the operation risked a nuclear response from the Kremlin. The following month, Musk published a four-point plan for peace in a post on Twitter. (He would buy the social network for $44 billion a few weeks later.) His peace plan hewed closely to Russian demands, including a provision for Ukraine to remain “neutral” after the war. In response, Zelensky posted his own Twitter survey , asking whether people preferred the Musk who supports Ukraine or the one who supports Russia. Andriy Melnyk, who served as Ukraine’s ambassador to Germany at the time, also shot back at Musk’s peace plan: “Fuck off is my very diplomatic reply to you @elonmusk.” In Zelensky’s wartime government, the official who cultivated the strongest ties with Musk and SpaceX was Mykhailo Fedorov, the chief architect of the Ukrainian drone program. Early this year, while serving as minister of defense, Fedorov persuaded Musk to shut off the Starlink receivers that Russian forces had been using to fly their own drones in Ukraine. But Fedorov lost his job this month in a government reshuffle, which cost Ukraine its main point of contact with Musk. “Fedorov has a super constructive relationship with him,” a Ukrainian official told us. “So the timing is very bad to install a new minister.” [ Read: Elon Musk moves against the Russians in Ukraine ] One person close to Fedorov told us that, in the weeks before he was fired, the minister lobbied Musk and various other contacts in the U.S. to allow the use of Starlink for drone strikes into Russia. Fedorov received assurances from Musk that it would be possible “if Trump says to do it,” the person said. The talks broke off, he added, after the government reshuffle. (Fedorov did not respond to a request for comment.) The Trump administration could have its own reasons to balk at Zelensky’s request. “It’s one thing to let Ukraine do this on its own territory,” the Ukrainian official said. “It’s another thing to use American technology on the territory of Russia to take out their air defenses, their launchers for ballistic missiles. This is an unfriendly act. I don’t know how Russia could react to that.” Russia recently deployed new methods for interfering with Starlink signals in Ukraine. Earlier this month, a set of documents was published that appeared to show Russia plotting with China to destroy Starlink satellites, through either hacking, jamming, or knocking them out of orbit. The documents, allegedly produced by China and obtained by The Insider , highlighted the risks Musk faces in helping Ukraine fight the war. His willingness to broaden that assistance could depend on the leverage Trump has over Musk—and his desire to use it for Ukraine’s benefit. Earlier this month, Trump seemed open to Zelensky’s strategy for pressuring Russia to negotiate a peace deal. “It’s an escalation,” Trump said when asked about Ukraine’s strikes on oil refineries and military targets deep inside Russia. Seated beside Zelensky in Ankara, Trump added: “But it’s also an escalation that could help lead to an end.”

items.title: Article attentatoires de « Maroc Hebdo » sur l’honneur des joueuses burkinabè : La Fédération burkinabè de football riposte énergiquement
items.description: La Fédération burkinabè de football (FBF) a réagi avec vigueur pour éteindre une polémique naissante. Dans un communiqué officiel publié ce 30 juillet 2026, l’instance faîtière du football national a opposé un démenti catégorique aux rumeurs d’abus sexuels qui auraient visé les joueuses de l’équipe nationale féminine, les Étalons Dames, lors de leur récente « immersion patriotique ». Qualifiant ces allégations, attribuées à une publication de Maroc Hebdo , de « totalement infondées », la FBF dénonce une attaque directe contre l’honneur des sportives et des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS). Déterminée à protéger l’intégrité du sport burkinabè, la fédération se réserve désormais le droit d’engager des poursuites judiciaires contre les auteurs de ces publications. L'honneur du football féminin burkinabè est au centre d'un bras de fer médiatique. Suite à la diffusion d'informations faisant état de prétendus abus sexuels subis par les Étalons Dames, la Fédération burkinabè de football a choisi la voie de la fermeté pour restaurer la vérité. Au cœur de cette affaire se trouve une publication attribuée à Maroc Hebdo , relatant des faits graves qui se seraient déroulés pendant la période d'immersion patriotique des joueuses. La réponse de la FBF est sans équivoque : ces allégations sont jugées « gravement attentatoires à l’honneur, à la dignité et à l’image des joueuses ». Pour l'institution, il ne s'agit pas seulement d'une attaque contre l'équipe, mais également contre leur encadrement et les Forces de défense et de sécurité qui ont accompagné le processus. Pour couper court aux spéculations, la Fédération a tenu à rappeler le cadre strict de l'« immersion patriotique ». Loin de toute zone d'ombre, cette étape s'inscrivait dans une démarche de formation civique et de renforcement de l’esprit de corps, sous l’encadrement de structures compétentes. « Elle s’est déroulée dans un cadre organisé », souligne le communiqué, balayant l'idée de dérives incontrôlées. Indignée par la diffusion de contenus dépourvus d'éléments vérifiables, la FBF appelle désormais les médias et les internautes à une plus grande responsabilité. Elle rappelle que la réputation des personnes est en jeu et invite le public à ne se fier qu'aux canaux officiels pour toute information relative à la sélection nationale féminine. La suite de cette affaire pourrait bien se jouer sur le terrain judiciaire. La Fédération a en effet annoncé qu'elle se réservait le droit d'engager « toute démarche appropriée » pour préserver les droits des institutions et des personnes injustement mises en cause. En réaffirmant son attachement absolu à la sécurité et à l'intégrité de ses joueuses, la FBF entend prouver que toute allégation d'abus est prise avec le plus grand sérieux, tout en refusant que l'image des Étalons Dames soit sacrifiée sur l'autel de contenus non vérifiés. items.title: ‘Ready to write Chelsea story’ – Lacroix makes £52m move
items.description: Chelsea have signed France’s World Cup defender Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace for £52m. The 26-year-old, capped seven times by France, has penned a contract at Stamford Bridge until 2032. The Frenchman joined Palace from Bundesliga side Wolfsburg in 2024 for an initial £15.5m and became a regular under Oliver Glasner last season. Lacroix made 55 appearances in all competitions as Palace won the Uefa Conference League , the club’s first major European trophy. The defender made three appearances for France during the 2026 World Cup, including against England in the third-place play-off, as Les Bleus finished fourth. “I think when I saw the players like Reece [James], like Morgan [Rogers], I’m just really happy to be also in a way in their story, you know? To write part of the Chelsea story with them,” Lacroix said. “I’m really proud, really happy, to be part of this beautiful project and I just want to start playing. “I’m really excited to see the guys, to see the manager, to start the season, because I feel like we have a story to write here, and I can be part of it, so it’s beautiful.” Lacroix is Chelsea ‘s third signing of the summer transfer window, joining Morgan Rogers and Marco Palestra in moving to west London, as the club prepares for its first season under new boss Xabi Alonso. Deals for winger Geovany Quenda and forward Emmanuel Emegha were agreed in 2025, with both players formally completing moves this month. The Blues are also currently in talks to sign Brighton striker Danny Welbeck and Brentford midfielder Jordan Henderson. ‘A ready-made signing’ – analysis Lacroix had been on a shortlist of centre-back options since it became clear Chelsea ‘s defence was underperforming and that they needed more physicality and leadership in their backline. Although former Manchester City defender John Stones and Como’s Jacobo Ramon were also known to be under consideration, it always felt as though the 6ft 4in Palace defender was Chelsea ‘s preferred target. Lengthy negotiations over both personal terms and the transfer fee with Crystal Palace added uncertainty to the deal. However, Lacroix gave the move the green light last week after France’s World Cup campaign ended with a fourth-place finish following defeat by England in the bronze-medal match. The signing offers a glimpse into Chelsea ‘s future direction after a season in which they finished 10th in the Premier League and ended the campaign without a trophy, prompting frustration among supporters. Co-owner Behdad Eghbali said Chelsea would “tweak” their model and add experience to what he still believes is a strong core of young players including Cole Palmer, Moises Caicedo and Levi Colwill. Not only is Lacroix the oldest player signed under the current ownership since Eghbali and his sporting directors took control, but Chelsea also attempted to sign Granit Xhaka, 34, from Sunderland in a deal that would have been highly unusual for the club’s recruitment strategy. Although Chelsea were unable to reunite the Switzerland midfielder with his former Bayer Leverkusen manager Alonso, the attempt sent a clear message that the club’s approach is changing. Along with £117m arrival Rogers, who turned 24 on Saturday, Lacroix’s arrival means Chelsea have delivered on their pledge to make at least two ready-made signings.

items.title: Kwame Dadzie to host 6th Ghana Comedy Awards
items.description: Ghanaian media personality Kwame Dadzie has been named host of the sixth edition of the Ghana Comedy Awards, scheduled for Saturday, 1st August 2026, at the Ghana College of Physicians and Surgeons in Ridge, Accra. The awards, organised by Creative Republic Limited, celebrate excellence in Ghana’s comedy industry by recognising outstanding comedians and other contributors whose work has made an impact over the past year. This year’s ceremony forms part of what organisers have described as Ghana’s biggest comedy festival. Kwame Dadzie, an arts and culture journalist with the Multimedia Group Limited, is best known as host of Showbiz A-Z on Joy FM and for his extensive coverage of Ghana’s creative industry. Over the years, he has built a reputation as one of the country’s leading entertainment journalists, covering music, film, theatre, literature and comedy, while also serving as a moderator and host for major entertainment events. He is also co-host of Ghana’s premier entertainment and lifestyle morning show Daybreak Hitz on Hitz FM. Apart from his forte in digging deep into entertainment issues, Kwame is known for his witty and comical antics, a rare quality that sets him apart from his peers. The 2026 Ghana Comedy Awards will honour comedians and industry players whose work stood out between 1st January and 31st December 2025. Award categories include comedy actor of the year, comedy actress of the year, comic writer of the year and comic TV/radio programme of the year. Beyond the awards presentations, patrons can expect performances from comedians including Lekzy, Jeneral Ntatia, Kojo PJay, Oh Joo, Alo Wess, Ranzy Ray and Jerry Ashinyo, alongside musical performances. On the red carpet with be Sheila Sakyi of Joy Prime and comic actor Pilato. The event begins with a red carpet session at 7:00 p.m., followed by the main awards ceremony at 8:30 p.m. Tickets are selling at GH¢200 for Silver and GH¢300 for Gold. Voting for nominees closes at 6:00 a.m. on Saturday, 1st August 2026.

À bord de l'Ocean Viking, les rescapés racontent les sévices sur les routes de l'exil
items.description: Depuis le début du mois de juillet, RFI s’est embarqué à bord de l’Ocean Viking, le bateau de sauvetage affrété par l’ONG française SOS Méditerranée. Patrouillant dans les eaux internationales au large de la Libye, le navire humanitaire a effectué samedi 18 juillet son premier sauvetage de l’été. L’équipage a secouru 38 migrants principalement issus d’Érythrée, du Soudan et de Somalie. Sous un soleil de plomb, sans eau et quasiment à court de carburant, ils voguaient sur une barque de fortune, en fer rouillé, qui menaçait de chavirer à tout moment. Une fois sains et saufs à bord de l’Ocean Viking, ces naufragés de la Méditerranée racontent leur périple, et comment ils en sont venus à prendre autant de risques pour fuir la violence, la torture et la guerre.

items.title: Kanye West: esto podía haber sido un ‘reel’

Alguien tiene una idea genial para una sección. Pero ¿podremos hacer dos años de eso? Nadie preguntó esto a West cuando se le ocurrió esto de sostener una veintena de temas desde la cima del mundo, sin más que una ayuda puntual de Andre’ Troutman, muchas luces y algún que otro fuego artificial. items.title: Premier League clubs agree EFL funding proposal
items.description: An end is finally in sight to the long-running funding dispute between the Premier League and the English Football League. The Premier League confirmed its 20 clubs have “unanimously voted” to approve a proposal for a “new strategic partnership”, which will be put to the EFL for its members to vote on in the next few days. No figure has been put on the deal, which is due to last 10 years, with both sides keen not to debate the issue in public. On Saturday, Sky News reported the figure as £1.5bn. This has not been confirmed or denied by the Premier League. The Premier League says the proposal is fully funded. It is expected to come through a transfer levy. “The Premier League already has long-term funding commitments to invest a record £1.6billion every three years into the wider game and communities,” said the Premier League. “The Premier League remains committed to finding a football-led solution and looks forward to continuing discussions with the EFL on progressing this proposal.” The funding row has been rumbling on since a fan-led review in 2021, which was commissioned by the government following a number of crises in the sport, including the failed European Super League project and the collapse of Bury FC. On a number of occasions, it has seemed a deal was close. In March 2024, the Premier League was warned by government officials that if it and the EFL failed to agree a deal, one would be imposed on them. On Tuesday, representatives of the Premier League, the EFL and the new Independent Regulator met to discuss the outline of a deal. “The EFL notes the Premier League’s position following its meeting with clubs earlier today, and now looks forward to receiving its formal proposal for consideration,” said the EFL. “This follows constructive discussions involving the EFL, Premier League and Independent Football Regulator over recent months. “The EFL Board will then review the full detail of the proposal, including its potential benefits, implications and alignment with the long-term interests of our 72 clubs, ahead of further dialogue with the Premier League. “The proposal will then be discussed in detail with our member clubs to determine next steps.” Resistance within the Premier League simply to hand over money was based on a number of factors, including the basic reality they would providing funds to clubs trying to replace them. In other instances, specifically Stoke City, EFL clubs have owners richer than some in the Premier League.

items.title: ESUT imposes N500,000 penalty on reckless driving after final exams
items.description: The Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) has imposed N500,000 penalty on any student driving recklessly within and around its premises after completing final examinations. ESUT’s Registrar, Mr Ambrose Ugwu, made the disclosure on Thursday while addressing members of the university community. Ugwu said that the measure was part of efforts to curb accidents and protect lives, due to reckless driving from students who celebrate the completion of their final examinations. “The reckless driving have caused incessant injuries and we urge students to leave quietly after writing their examinations. “Any vehicle impounded over such anomaly will pay N500,000 penalty. “The directive commences from July 31 and is being made to the notice of students who will complete their final examinations then,” he said. The registrar said that the prohibition remained in force in compliance with the resolution of the Enugu State House of Assembly on such issue. “The directive has also been earlier conveyed by the state commissioner for education in a memo dated Dec. 20, 2024 and addressed to the institution’s vice-chancellor. “The university warns that it would not hesitate to take drastic actions against students violating the directive. “Any vehicle impounded for reckless driving wil not be released until the owner pays a penalty of N500,000. “The student found culpable will face additional disciplinary sanctions in line with the institution’s regulations,” he said. Ugwu said that the directive mandated all deans, directors and heads of departments to sensitise and warn their final-year students to strictly comply with the directive. “The institution’s chief security officer and other law enforcement agencies are mandated to be vigilant and ensure that law and order are maintained throughout the university premises. “Members of the university community are enjoined to be guided accordingly and comply fully with the directive. “The university remains resolute to enforce the ban in ensuring the safety of lives and property on campus.” (NAN) The post ESUT imposes N500,000 penalty on reckless driving after final exams appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tunisie | L’ANCS met en garde contre des SMS d’hameçonnage ciblant les automobilistes
items.description: L'Agence nationale de la sécurité cybernétique (ANCS) a émis une alerte urgente concernant une vague de campagnes de phishing (hameçonnage) circulant actuellement par SMS. Selon l'alerte de l'ANCS, les victimes reçoivent des SMS provenant de numéros étrangers signalant de fausses infractions routières non payées. Ces messages contiennent un lien menant vers une fausse plateforme présentée comme officielle, afin d'inciter l'utilisateur à régler la prétendue amende. Cette manœuvre vise à voler les données bancaires et personnelles des usagers une fois connectés au faux site. L'ANCS rappelle à tous les citoyens que les sites gouvernementaux officiels utilisent exclusivement le domaine .tn . L'Agence appelle par ailleurs à la plus grande vigilance et recommande de ne jamais cliquer sur des liens issus de numéros étrangers ou suspects. Y. N. items.title: Conseil des ministres : Santé, eau, électricité, éducation …, le Burkina Faso acte le transfert massif de compétences vers les collectivités territoriales
items.description: Une étape majeure de la réforme de l’État burkinabè vient d’être franchie. Réuni en séance ordinaire ce jeudi 30 juillet 2026 sous la présidence du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le Conseil des ministres a adopté une série de douze décrets stratégiques, dont onze consacrent le transfert effectif de compétences et de ressources vers les collectivités territoriales. Couvrant des domaines aussi vitaux que la santé, l’eau, l’éducation ou la gestion foncière, ces mesures visent une gestion plus efficiente des ressources publiques au plus près des besoins des populations. Parallèlement, le gouvernement a acté la création d’un registre national des chefs coutumiers, marquant une volonté de sécuriser et de clarifier le statut de la chefferie traditionnelle dans le cadre de la transition institutionnelle du pays. Le Conseil des ministres du 30 juillet 2026 restera sans doute comme un pivot dans l'histoire de la décentralisation au Burkina Faso. Pendant près de quatre heures, le gouvernement, sous la direction du Chef de l'État, a délibéré sur une architecture juridique destinée à transformer en profondeur la gouvernance locale. L’une des décisions phares concerne la mise en œuvre de la loi sur le statut de la chefferie coutumière et traditionnelle. Le Conseil a adopté un décret fixant le contenu d'un registre national dédié à ces autorités. Ce référentiel officiel ne servira pas seulement à répertorier les chefs ; il doit favoriser la sécurisation des informations administratives et garantir une traçabilité rigoureuse des successions, reconnaissances ou vacances de chefferie. C’est, pour l’exécutif, un moyen de disposer de statistiques fiables et d'éviter les conflits de légitimité. Le cœur de cette séance a toutefois été marqué par l’adoption de dix décrets organisant le transfert de compétences et de ressources de l’État vers les communes et les régions. Ce mouvement d’envergure touche la quasi-totalité des secteurs de la vie sociale et économique : Services sociaux de base : La santé, l’hygiène, l’eau, l’assainissement et l’électricité passent sous une gestion locale accrue. Éducation et Jeunesse : Les domaines de l’emploi, de la formation professionnelle et de l’alphabétisation sont désormais transférés. Économie et Territoire : La gestion des marchés, des foires, des aires d’abattage, ainsi que l’aménagement urbain et la gestion foncière sont confiés aux collectivités. Identité et Citoyenneté : Le transfert inclut également les droits humains, la promotion du civisme et l’assistance humanitaire. Pour éviter tout chevauchement, un onzième décret définit un protocole d’opérationnalisation. Ce texte clarifie les engagements respectifs de l’État et des collectivités territoriales afin d’accroître la performance de la décentralisation. L’objectif est clair : améliorer la gouvernance locale en précisant les rôles et les responsabilités de chaque acteur. Enfin, le Conseil a clos ses travaux sur le volet mobilité en approuvant les nouveaux statuts de la Société de transport en commun (SOTRACO), lui permettant de se doter d'un cadre réglementaire moderne pour assurer ses missions de service public. Avec ces décisions, le Burkina Faso de la Transition s'engage résolument vers une administration territoriale plus autonome, responsable et tournée vers le développement endogène. items.title: Prince Amoako Jnr scores as Nordsjaelland cruise past GAIS in Conference League qualifier
items.description: Ghanaian youngster Prince Amoako Jnr was among the scorers as FC Nordsjaelland produced a dominant display to thrash Swedish side GAIS 6-0 in their UEFA Conference League qualifying clash on Thursday night. The 19-year-old winger continued his impressive start to the season by netting his side’s fifth goal of the evening, capping another influential performance for the Danish outfit. Nordsjaelland controlled proceedings from the opening whistle, enjoying 57 percent possession and dictating the tempo throughout the contest. The hosts created chance after chance, finishing with 22 shots, including 10 on target, while limiting GAIS to just 10 attempts, only two of which tested the goalkeeper. The Danish side raced into a commanding first-half lead through goals from Runar Robinson Norheim, Villum Berthelsen and Hjalte Boe Rasmussen, leaving the visitors with a mountain to climb before the interval. Norheim grabbed his second goal shortly after the restart before Amoako Jnr got his name on the scoresheet with a composed finish to make it 5-0, continuing his rich vein of form in front of goal. Nicklas Røjkjær completed the rout as Nordsjaelland wrapped up an emphatic victory to take a significant step towards the next round of the competition. Amoako Jnr’s latest goal adds to what has been a remarkable rise for the Right to Dream Academy graduate. The Ghanaian enjoyed a breakthrough campaign last season, registering eight goals and five assists in 31 appearances across all competitions, performances that earned him the club’s iconic No. 10 shirt. The teenager has also attracted growing interest from clubs across Europe, with JoySports previously reporting that Brighton & Hove Albion, PSV Eindhoven, Feyenoord and Coventry City are all monitoring the highly-rated winger. Nordsjaelland will now turn their attention to the Danish Superliga, where they face Randers on August 2, with Amoako Jnr hoping to carry his impressive form into the domestic campaign.

Minimum 10-match ban for discrimination – FA
items.description: Players found guilty of discrimination will face a ban of at least 10 matches under strengthened Football Association rules coming in for the new season. In previous seasons, suspensions ranged from six to 12 matches for ‘aggravated breaches’ of FA Rule E3.2, which relates to misconduct around references to ethnic origin, colour, race, nationality, religion, sex, gender, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, or disability. The strengthened sanction, which also applies to managers and individuals in the technical area, is part of the FA’s commitment to “delivering a game free from discrimination”. “While significant progress has been made in recent years, discriminatory conduct continues to be a challenge across the game,” an FA statement read. “Enhanced measured are necessary to tackle this abhorrent conduct.” A sanction above the new standard minimum 10-match suspension may be imposed by a regulatory commission if there are “significant” aggravating factors. Shorter bans – with a minimum of six matches – may also be considered when there are mitigating circumstances or an individual has admitted the breach at the earliest opportunity. But a six-match ban would now only be considered in those circumstances – rather than being the standard minimum suspension, as it was before. Individuals who are found to have committed two or more aggravated breaches on separate occasions may face a suspension in excess of 12 matches or time-based suspensions of any duration in “very serious cases”.

items.title: Ghana backs extending presidential term to 5 yrs, lowering age limit
items.description: Ghana’s government on Thursday accepted a proposal to extend the presidential term to five years and lower the minimum age for candidates to 35. Ghana, one of Africa’s leading gold and cocoa producers, has maintained a stable democratic system since 1992. President John Dramani Mahama established a committee last year to review the constitution. The committee submitted its final report to him on Thursday. “The government has accepted the recommendation to extend the term of office of the president from four years to five years,” Justice Minister Dominic Ayine told journalists. The committee said parliament’s term should also be increased to five years to align with the presidency. Although the committee recommended lowering the minimum age for presidential candidates to 30, Ayine said the government would instead adopt 35. The Constitution Review Committee said a four-year presidential cycle can leave an administration with “a little over two years” of effective governing time, as the first six months can be taken up by appointments and the final year by elections. It said a five-year term could also “strengthen democratic accountability” by giving governments more time to deliver. A national referendum in 2027 will be required to pass the changes, with strict voter turnout and approval thresholds. items.title: Tonali ‘took 10 minutes’ to decide to join Spurs
items.description: Club-record £100m signing Sandro Tonali took “10 minutes” to decide to join Tottenham from Newcastle after meeting manager Roberto de Zerbi at his home. The 26-year-old said a shared passion for his boyhood club Brescia played a key role in the move. De Zerbi grew up a Brescia fan and later played for them, while Tonali started his career there, and that connection helped pave the way for the biggest transfer in Tottenham ‘s history. “We spoke about Brescia, about the difficult situation facing our club,” Tonali said, referring to the bankruptcy of his boyhood side following relegation to Italy’s third tier. De Zerbi texted a mutual friend during last season to ask whether Tonali might be interested in joining Tottenham and was told: “He is open.” His immediate focus was securing Premier League survival and, the day after Tottenham beat Everton to avoid relegation, De Zerbi contacted Tonali about a potential move. Within 10 minutes, he had received a phone call from the midfielder. A further meeting at Tonali’s home, just outside Brescia, followed as talks progressed. “Brescia is so small. I had two weeks there and met him two or three times,” Tonali said. Tonali said his connection with De Zerbi stretches back nine years to the coach’s spell in charge of Sassuolo, when he wanted to sign him. That brief reign helped launch De Zerbi’s managerial career and began what Tonali described as a “mini-connection”. After their meeting this summer, however, he said he knew “everything” about his future manager. Sources close to Tonali described how those meetings had captivated him, despite interest from clubs with far stronger recent records than Spurs, who had finished 17th the previous season, allowing Tottenham to pull off a coup. Spurs were my best ‘solution’ “Honestly, I spoke with another team [also],” Tonali revealed, but in the end the decision to join Spurs was an easy one. “When you speak with a team, the first impression is a big thing and my impression was very positive. “When you are happy after a 10-minute chat, it’s everything, everything is perfect. “I spoke with my wife – this was the first thing. We wanted to change our life, but not just for the city, we wanted to change everything. We spoke with two clubs.” Tonali said moving to London represented about 10% of the attraction as he wanted his family to be happy, but said football, De Zerbi and Tottenham ‘s recruitment staff made up the other 90% of his decision. There was also further discussion about the transfer fee, what it means for him and Newcastle , and how it effectively priced him and his family out of a move back to Italy. “We had decided to come back in Italy but it was impossible for the money,” he admitted, explaining clubs could afford his wages but not the transfer fee. “England was our solution and we found the best solution in England for me, for my career, for my football, for my happiness, for my family. I spoke with two teams. I understood after 10, 15 minutes that Tottenham would be my next team.” At Spurs, he joins an Italian contingent within the coaching staff and links up with fellow Italy international Destiny Udogie, but he stressed the move was not motivated by any unhappiness during his time at Newcastle . Unprompted, he said: “Eddie [Howe] was fantastic for me”, adding that he wants to maintain a friendship with his former manager – who is also leaving the Magpies – and Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson. He went on to explain that he wanted “the best deal” for Newcastle because they “deserve everything”, while also praising the atmosphere at St James’ Park and the passion of the club’s supporters. Although not referenced directly, Tonali served a 10-month ban for breaches of FA betting rules during his time at Newcastle . His £100m price tag is also something Tonali admits will bring “a lot of pressure”, but he insists he will continue to behave as a “normal” Tottenham player and person in his private life. “I don’t know your impression about football players like me, but honestly, I’m a normal person. When I go back to Italy, I go to my family, to my grandma, to my friends. If it is perfect for my family, it is perfect for me,” he said.

items.title: Stray bullet shatters bystander’s right leg in Wechiau clashes, MP demands swift justice
items.description: A 24-year-old bystander has sustained a severe gunshot injury to his right thigh during renewed clashes between civilians and police in Wechiau in the Wa West District. The incident has renewed concerns over the protracted communal conflict in the area, with Member of Parliament for Wa West, Peter Lanchene Toobu, calling for an immediate end to the violence and a swift, impartial investigation by state security agencies. The latest victim, Babuule Wahidu, was allegedly hit by a stray bullet while attempting to conduct a mobile money transaction. According to Dr Philip K.K. Baabiineh, a trauma and orthopaedic surgeon at the Upper West Regional Hospital, Mr Wahidu was rushed to the facility in critical condition and required urgent surgery. “He alleged that he was at a mobile money vendor to do a cash out. While he was there, he saw people running and then he also turned to run. Before he could say Jack, a bullet entered his leg,” Dr Baabiineh explained. Medical staff stabilised Mr Wahidu before performing surgery to treat the injury. The surgeon said the victim suffered a penetrating injury consistent with a gunshot wound on the outer side of his right thigh. “Luckily, the bones were intact. So we went and explored the wound, removed the foreign body that was there, debrided, and did the necessary procedures,” he said. Mr Wahidu is currently recovering at the hospital and is receiving antibiotics, with doctors hopeful that he could be discharged within a week. A second victim who sustained a gunshot wound to the shoulder during the clashes is also reported to be in stable condition and is being managed without surgery. The latest casualties add to the growing tensions surrounding the Lassia Tuolu-Kendeu conflict, which began on June 15, 2024, after years of peaceful coexistence between the communities were disrupted. The conflict has so far resulted in deaths, destruction of property and deepened tensions within the district. Addressing the media in Wa following a fact-finding visit to Wechiau, Mr Toobu expressed concern about the impact of the violence on residents and the district’s development. “The incident left many families devastated and threatened the peace and stability of our beloved district,” he said. The MP warned that continued cycles of violence and retaliation were undermining the future of young people and diverting resources that could have been invested in development. He noted that mediation efforts had been making progress until November 23, 2025, when two young men from Bakpaateng were killed near Lassia Tuolu. Tensions escalated further following the death of a prime suspect, Tijjani Abu, while in police custody at the SDA Hospital in Wa on July 25, 2026. Mr Toobu has since called on the Ghana Police Service and the Attorney-General’s Office to expedite investigations into both the clashes and the custodial death. “It is my sincere hope that these painful deaths will become the last sacrifices in our collective search for lasting peace, justice, reconciliation, and social cohesion,” he said. “Justice delayed is justice denied.”

items.title: Abandon Hope, All Ye Who Enter the Mar-a-Lago in Heaven
items.description: Lindsey, Mr. President, I would argue in my mind, probably has a heavenly version of Mar-a-Lago. It may even be a little bigger. He may have a little more gold in the Oval Office in his mansion in heaven, and I wouldn’t be surprised if he added one big, beautiful ballroom and an arch somewhere on the property because he would want to obviously duplicate his dearest friend in life, you, Mr. President. — Sean Hannity, at Senator Lindsey Graham’s funeral The Mar-a-Lago in heaven is even bigger than it looks. But it’s less crowded than it might be, considering that it’s the Mar-a-Lago in heaven . Look at the chip-and-putt golf course! Admire the vista stretching from the sea to the lake. There is croquet. There is European-style terrace dining. And six tennis courts! Or pull back from Mar-a-Lago and observe the Reflecting Pool (perfectly American-flag blue), the arch, the Oval Office. This is it—the perfect way to spend eternity! It isn’t an insult to consign a soul to Mar-a-Lago for all time. This premier final destination received the “coveted” Six Star Diamond Award for its “leading hospitality” in 2008—a fact that the club’s website still boasts. Just look at the amenities. The food here is the best. The chocolate cake at the Mar-a-Lago in heaven is even better than the one Xi Jinping enjoyed at the Mar-a-Lago on Earth while President Trump talked about bombing Syria. (You can’t drop bombs from here, but there is a button you can press for unlimited Diet Cokes.) Many such treats are available! Enjoy the president’s playlist, the most wonderful playlist in the world: The Phantom of the Opera and “Nessun dorma” and “Tiny Dancer” and “Y.M.C.A.” They never tire of playing “Y.M.C.A.”! It is heaven, after all. For entertainment, giant TVs play Hannity and Meet the Press , 24/7! Or if you want to read, you’re in luck: There are classified documents too, lying around in cardboard boxes. You can spend forever paging through them if you like. If you get bored of state secrets, visit the ballroom. It is so big and so secure, secure as a fortification. To keep something out? Or to keep something in? No, no one would ever wish to escape this heaven, a heaven interior-decorated according to the wishes of Donald J. Trump. It is good to be here for all eternity. Sometimes the sky gets very thick with smog, but that is just because they are burning clean coal. No horrible windmills here! Sometimes you hear coughing, but that isn’t your concern. How long has it been since you heard birdsong or genuine, unfeigned laughter? No matter—why don’t you admire the gold finishings? So many gold finishings! Just when you think you are done admiring them, more sprout up! You can also admire the arch, or what you can see of it. It’s huge, too tall for you to make out the top. It seems to pierce through the roof of heaven itself. Looking at it makes you feel dizzy and disoriented, and you start to feel that you cannot tell up from down. Are you looking down from a great height or up at a great height? Where is your compass? You should have packed your compass! No! It is all right. You are all right. Only a true compass could have steered you to such an exclusive place as this. Mar-a-Lago is heaven, and heaven would be incomplete without Mar-a-Lago. To say so is not to flatter power but to speak from your heart, as Sean Hannity knows. And in heaven a true heart is always rewarded. And so, of course, here you are. Perfect bliss, after all, to spend eternity haunting another man’s marble halls. Better to reign in hell than serve in heaven? That’s the devil talking! He didn’t know Mar-a-Lago was an option.

items.title: El Gobierno moviliza al Ejército de Tierra desplegado en Ceuta y cierra la frontera con Melilla
items.description: La situación de máxima tensión que se vive en Ceuta por la crisis migratoria, que ha dejado al menos dieciocho víctimas mortales, ha desbordado este jueves todas las previsiones del Gobierno. La entrada de miles de inmigrantes ha provocado que España y Marruecos acuerden “reforzar la coordinación” y los esfuerzos para hacer frente al cruce descontrolado en la ciudad autónoma, donde han llegado entre 1.500 y 2.000 personas en los últimos 10 días, y se han comprometido a revisar e implementar medidas para la entrega, “lo antes posible, de todas las que han entrado ilegalmente”, según ha informado Interior en un comunicado y han confirmado también fuentes marroquíes a la Agencia Efe. Desde La Moncloa, además, se ha movilizado a última hora de la tarde a las unidades del Ejército de Tierra desplegadas en Ceuta para apoyar a los efectivos de la Guardia Civil que se encuentran sobrepasados, como ya ocurrió en 2021. Horas después, el Ejecutivo ha cerrado la frontera con Melilla tras un intento de entrada por Beni Enzar. Y el presidente Pedro Sánchez viajará este viernes a la ciudad autónoma ante la magnitud de la emergencia. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Máxima alerta en Ceuta tras el cruce descontrolado de miles de personas desde Marruecos que deja al menos 18 muertos
items.description: Miles de personas han cruzado sin control de Marruecos a Ceuta el mediodía de este jueves, caminando en tierra firme primero y sorteando a nado el espigón que marca la frontera. La madrugada, que había sido tranquila, con decenas de entradas a nado, se ha desbordado a mediodía. Los marroquíes eran una manifestación de miles de personas que entraban mojados y victoriosos como si celebraran un mundial. Se abrazan, piden ropa limpia para secar el móvil, gritan de alborozo, los unos. Otros, con los niños en brazos, siguen el camino buscando quizá el centro de acogida. La Guardia Civil y los medios de emergencia, superados, solo intentan ocuparse de los heridos. Al menos dieciocho personas han muerto intentando llegar. El Gobierno ha movilizado a última hora de la tarde a las unidades del Ejército de Tierra desplegadas en Ceuta para apoyar a los efectivos del instituto armado y el presidente Pedro Sánchez viajará este viernes a la ciudad autónoma. items.title: Court ends 13-years amputee football dispute as high court rules in favour of NSA and NPC Ghana
items.description: One of the longest-running and most fiercely contested legal battles in Ghanaian sports has finally come to an end after the High Court delivered a landmark judgment that decisively settles the governance of amputee football in Ghana. In a ruling expected to reshape the future administration of the sport, the High Court found in favour of the National Sports Authority (NSA) and the National Paralympic Committee (NPC) Ghana, affirming their authority over the governance and recognition of amputee football under Ghana’s national sports framework. Delivering judgment in the case Ghana Amputee Football Federation v. National Sports Authority & Others in Commercial Court 6, Justice Jerome Noble-Nkrumah, JA, dismissed the plaintiffs’ claims in their entirety, holding that the case presented by the National Sports Authority and NPC Ghana was more probable. The Court consequently granted the reliefs sought in the defendants’ counterclaim. The Court also awarded GH¢60,000 in costs to each of the National Sports Authority and NPC Ghana, although the two institutions had respectively sought GH¢250,000 and GH¢200,000. In one of the most significant aspects of the ruling, the Court granted reliefs that include perpetual orders affecting the Ghana Amputee Football Federation (GAFF) and Francis Adjetey Sowah, Charles Narh Teye, John Kuku Dsane, Philip Cecil Richter and Benjamin Charles Armah, in accordance with the terms of the judgment not to associate themselves with Amputee sport in Ghana. The decision effectively ends a dispute that has dominated amputee football administration in Ghana for well over a decade. Court records, official correspondence, witness statements and institutional documents reviewed in connection with the proceedings indicate that the dispute dates back to 2013–2014, when disagreements emerged regarding which institution possessed the lawful mandate to administer amputee football in Ghana. Over the years, the disagreement evolved into one of Ghana’s most protracted sports governance disputes, involving multiple court proceedings, competing institutional claims, government intervention and correspondence involving international sporting bodies. The litigation centred on critical questions concerning which institution possessed the legal mandate to administer amputee football in Ghana, the legal recognition of competing organisations, the legitimacy of governance structures and elections, and the authority of Ghana’s national sports institutions under the country’s sports governance framework. Throughout the proceedings, the National Sports Authority and NPC Ghana consistently maintained that amputee football falls within Ghana’s recognized national sports governance architecture. The documentary record further shows that while the substantive case remained pending, the Commercial Division of the High Court directed the then Ministry of Youth and Sports to develop measures to ensure Ghana’s participation in international amputee football competitions. Following submissions by the Ministry, the Court approved a structured roadmap that enabled Ghana to compete at the Amputee Football World Cup while preserving the integrity of the pending litigation. The implementation of that roadmap was supervised by the Ministry with recognized roles assigned to the Samson Deen’s Led NPC Ghana. The judgment marks a defining moment for sports governance in Ghana. By resolving years of uncertainty over institutional authority, the ruling is expected to provide greater administrative clarity, reinforce the country’s sports governance framework and allow stakeholders to concentrate on athlete development, international competitiveness and the long-term growth of amputee football. With the legal dispute now concluded, attention is expected to shift from courtroom battles to rebuilding the sport, strengthening governance structures and creating a united platform to advance opportunities for Ghana’s amputee footballers both at home and on the international stage. A detailed analysis of the Court’s judgment and its legal implications for sports governance in Ghana will follow after the full written decision has been reviewed.

items.title: CAN Féminine : Le Maroc dompte l'Algérie et se qualifie pour les quarts de finale
items.description: *]:pointer-events-auto R6Vx5W_threadScrollVars scroll-mb-[calc(var(--scroll-root-safe-area-inset-bottom,0px)+var(--thread-response-height))] scroll-mt-[calc(var(--header-height)+min(200px,max(70px,20svh)))]" dir="auto" data-turn-id="request-WEB:d900d699-86a0-4921-9268-ca0e4b7a22c1-0" data-turn-id-container="request-WEB:d900d699-86a0-4921-9268-ca0e4b7a22c1-0" data-testid="conversation-turn-2" data-turn="assistant"> L’équipe nationale féminine de football s’est imposée face à son homologue algérienne sur le score de 1 but à 0, en match de la 2e journée du groupe A de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations féminine Maroc-2026, disputé jeudi soir au Stade Moulay El Hassan à Rabat. A l’entame de la rencontre, les deux équipes ont déroulé un jeu marqué par la prudence pour éviter d’encaisser le premier but, avant que les Lionnes de l'Atlas ne prennent l'initiative et imposer leur style de jeu en construisant des attaques structurées à travers les flancs pour créer des espaces au sein de la ligne défensive algérienne. Les protégées de Jorge Vilda ont tenté de porter le danger sur le but de la gardienne algérienne Chloé N'Gazi par le biais de Sakina Ouzraoui sur l'aile droite et Sanaa Mssoudy sur l'aile gauche, tandis que le milieu de terrain, composé de Yasmine Mrabet, Kautar Azraf et Elodie Nakkach, s'est appliqué à sécuriser la construction du jeu et à récupérer rapidement le ballon pour relancer les attaques. La première occasion dangereuse est survenue à la 17e minute, à la suite d'un coup de pied arrêté tiré dans la surface de réparation par Kautar Azraf, repris d'une tête de Nouhaila Benzina qui a frôlé les filets de l'équipe algérienne. Les Lionnes de l’Atlas ont poursuivi la maîtrise du tempo de la rencontre, portées par les supporters marocains venus en nombre. De son côté, la sélection algérienne a dû attendre la 37e minute pour signer sa première tentative via une frappe depuis l'extérieur de la surface de réparation, sans danger pour la gardienne Khadija Er-Rmichi. La première mi-temps s'est ainsi achevée sur un score nul et vierge. A la reprise, les Lionnes de l’Atlas ont accentué la pression sur la ligne défensive algérienne pour faire sauter le verrou, notamment par le biais de Zineb Redouani et Ibtissam Jraidi. L’entrée en jeu de la capitaine Ghizlane Chebbak en remplacement de Ibtissam Jraidi (70e) a dynamisé le jeu des Lionnes de l’Atlas qui sont montées au créneau pour prendre l’avantage. Sanaa Mssoudy (75e) a tenté d’ouvrir le score d’une frappe de la tête, après un coup arrêté exécuté par Chebbak, repoussée par la gardienne algérienne. Le but de la délivrance est intervenu par Sanaa Mssoudy à la 84e minute de jeu. Au terme de la 2e journée, le Maroc occupe la tête du groupe A avec 6 unités, suivi de l’Algérie (3 pts), du Sénégal (3 pts) et du Kenya (0 pt). items.title: Newcastle captain Guimaraes expected to join Arsenal
items.description: There is growing expectation that Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes will join Arsenal this summer, multiple sources have told BBC Sport. The Brazil midfielder has made it clear he wants to join the Premier League champions and Arsenal are increasingly confident of signing the 28-year-old. Guimaraes, who has scored 31 goals in 195 appearances for Newcastle since joining from Lyon in 2022 , has been a player of interest to the Gunners all summer. Arsenal will need to improve the £70m bid they made this month if they are to sign Guimaraes, who is due to return to Newcastle training in the coming days. Sources insists a new proposal is yet to be submitted, while Newcastle are adamant that formal club-to-club talks over Guimaraes’ protracted switch to north London have not taken place. Nevertheless, Arsenal are aiming to agree a deal in the coming days which could reach £80m. The belief that a move is within reach is not related to Eddie Howe’s decision to step down as Newcastle head coach. Arsenal were interested in signing Morgan Rogers, who has joined Chelsea for £117m, from Aston Villa – but refused to go higher than their £80m valuation. It is understood Arsenal were given the opportunity to match Chelsea ‘s offer for Rogers but declined. Newcastle , meanwhile, now face losing another key player, with Sandro Tonali having joined Tottenham and Anthony Gordon moving to Barcelona. Howe left Newcastle on Thursday after five years in charge, with Matthias Jaissle, manager of Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli , expected to be appointed his successor.

items.title: Tivaouane : Le préfet annonce l’arrêt des travaux d’assainissement des eaux pluviales pour le 14 août
items.description: Le préfet de Tivaouane, Abou Sow, a annoncé l’arrêt des travaux d’assainissement des eaux pluviales pour le 14 août 2026. À moins d’un mois du Gamou, le comité de suivi a effectué une visite de terrain ce jeudi 30 juillet. Objectif : boucler les chantiers, réhabiliter les routes et rétablir les réseaux d’eau et d’électricité fortement impactés. TIVAOUANE- Ce jeudi 30 juillet, le préfet du département de Tivaouane, Abou Sow, président du comité de suivi, a conduit une visite des chantiers d’assainissement. Il a annoncé l’arrêt des travaux lancés par l’État du Sénégal en novembre 2025, en prélude au Gamou annuel. Le comité s’est d’abord rendu dans les zones sensibles. À Keur Baïty Balla Dia, l’éclatement d’un tuyau d’eaux usées de l’ONAS avait causé des dégâts et menacé quelques maisons d’effondrement. « La situation est heureusement maîtrisée », a rassuré le préfet. L’entreprise Kelimane et l’Office national de l’assainissement du Sénégal ont pompé l’eau et rétabli la situation. Le préfet a insisté sur trois priorités avant le Gamou : la réhabilitation des routes en accélérant les travaux pour faciliter la fluidité de la circulation avant la période du Burd et, au plus tard, avant le Gamou. La fermeture des tuyaux ouverts, dont les conduites au niveau de la corniche, avant le 14 août afin de donner un meilleur visage à la cité religieuse, mais aussi le rétablissement des réseaux pour leur entretien concernant Sen’Eau et la Senelec, puisque leurs réseaux ont été fortement endommagés par les travaux d’assainissement. Le problème du manque d’eau a été au cœur des discussions. Les dégâts sur le réseau de Sen’Eau ont privé plusieurs quartiers d’eau. Les camions-citernes mobilisés pour Keur Baïty Balla et les autres zones touchées « ne suffisent plus », selon Abou Sow. Le préfet a recommandé l’installation de robinets publics en attendant la réhabilitation complète du réseau. Ibrahima NDIAYE (Correspondant)

items.title: Japa: Violence against doctors fuels brain drain in Nigeria – Ogun NMA
items.description: .says Ogun needs at least 5,000 physicians By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), Ogun State branch, has raised alarm over the increasing harassment, intimidation and physical assaults on doctors, warning that the trend is worsening the country’s brain drain crisis and threatening healthcare delivery. Speaking at a press conference in Abeokuta on Thursday, as part of activities marking the association’s 2026 Annual General Meeting (AGM), the Chairman of the Ogun State chapter, Dr. Ogunjimi Luqman Opeoluwa, said the association chose the theme, “Protecting the Doctor, Caring for the Caregiver,” in response to the growing wave of attacks on medical practitioners across the State and Nigeria. He said, healthcare workers who dedicate their lives to saving others deserve protection rather than violence. “We chose this theme because of the continuous and sustained harassment and physical assaults directed at doctors in various centres across Ogun State and, indeed, Nigeria. These incidents have become increasingly rampant. Healthcare providers who devote their lives to caring for others urgently need greater protection. Their safety must be a priority,” he said. Dr. Ogunjimi disclosed that Ogun State, with an estimated population of about nine million people, currently has only about 1,200 doctors serving in federal and state public health institutions. According to him, the figure is grossly inadequate for the healthcare needs of the state’s growing population. “We have only about 1,200 doctors serving a population of nine million people. That translates to roughly one doctor for every 7,500 residents. We are not where we should be, but those who remain have chosen to stay and serve their country despite enormous challenges.” The NMA chairman said the state requires between 5,000 and 10,000 doctors to provide effective healthcare services. “If Ogun State had between 5,000 and 10,000 doctors, that would be a much better situation. Modern healthcare is multidisciplinary. A single patient may require the expertise of several specialists before recovery. That is why we need many more doctors.” The association expressed concern over what it described as the increasing involvement of security agencies in matters relating to medical practice without first allowing professional regulatory processes to take their course. Dr. Ogunjimi insisted that allegations of medical negligence should first be investigated by the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN), which is statutorily empowered to examine professional misconduct. “When a doctor is accused of professional negligence, there is a legally established body responsible for investigating such matters; the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria. What we object to is the growing trend of security agencies arresting and prosecuting doctors without following due process.” He lamented that doctors, particularly those working in border communities such as Ota, Mowe and Ogijo, are frequently arrested following the death of patients without proper investigations into the circumstances surrounding the cases. “Doctors should not be arrested simply because a patient dies. Medical diagnosis and treatment are continuous processes. Before concluding that negligence occurred, investigators should understand the patient’s medical history, the nature of the illness and the care provided.” The NMA chairman revealed that the association had repeatedly accompanied doctors to police stations over matters that should ordinarily have been handled through established professional procedures. He further disclosed that the association currently has three assault cases before the courts after insisting that perpetrators of attacks on healthcare workers be prosecuted. Appealing to members of the public, Dr. Ogunjimi urged patients and their relatives to utilise existing complaint mechanisms within hospitals rather than resorting to violence. He noted that hospitals have established channels, including SERVICOM units, to investigate complaints against healthcare workers. “If anyone is dissatisfied with the care received, there are established complaint channels within our hospitals. Resorting to physical assault against doctors or other healthcare workers is completely unacceptable.” He stressed that while doctors remain committed to providing quality medical care, they cannot guarantee every clinical outcome. “We care deeply about our patients, but ultimately, healing comes from God. We are not God, and we cannot guarantee every outcome.” The association acknowledged that the migration of doctors abroad remains a major concern but maintained that many medical practitioners have deliberately chosen to remain in Nigeria. “Brain drain is a serious problem, but some of us have made a conscious decision to remain here and contribute our quota. What we are asking of government and the public is to take good care of those who have decided to stay.” Dr. Ogunjimi appealed to government at all levels to prioritise the welfare of healthcare workers to encourage retention of skilled professionals. Despite identifying several welfare gaps, the NMA commended the Ogun State government for implementing key financial incentives for doctors. The chairman specifically praised Governor Dapo Abiodun for approving and commencing the payment of the Professional Allowance Table (PAT) in line with the Federal Government structure, as well as the payment of the Specialist Allowance effective from July 2026. He also acknowledged previous achievements secured through dialogue with the government, including payment of the revised Consolidated Medical Salary Structure (CONMESS), clinical duty allowances for honorary consultants at Olabisi Onabanjo University Teaching Hospital, regular payment of accoutrement allowance and the Medical Residency Training Fund. “One of the positive steps taken by the governor was the approval and implementation of the new allowance. While there are still significant gaps, we commend the government for the progress made and encourage it to do more.” The NMA appealed to the State government to consider tax reforms for medical practitioners, particularly those in private practice. According to the association, doctors currently face multiple taxation from different government agencies, creating unnecessary financial burdens. “Private practitioners face the challenge of multiple taxation. Different agencies impose various levies. These taxes should be consolidated into a single unified payment system.” The post Japa: Violence against doctors fuels brain drain in Nigeria – Ogun NMA appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Defender Stones joins Inter Milan on free transfer
items.description: England defender John Stones has joined Italian champions Inter Milan on a free transfer and signed a two-year contract. The 32-year-old left Manchester City when his deal expired at the end of June after 10 successful years at the Premier League club. Stones said he had “lived all my dreams out” after helping City win six Premier League titles, the Champions League, two FA Cups, five League Cups, three Community Shields, the Club World Cup and the Uefa Super Cup. Since he became a free agent, the centre-back has attracted interest from clubs across Europe, including Chelsea and Juventus. Inter Milan were crowned Serie A champions for the 21st time last season and will start their title defence against newly promoted Monza on Saturday, 22 August. Former Barnsley defender Stones made 295 appearances for City, scoring 19 goals, after joining from Everton for £47.5m in 2016. He has won 93 caps and was part of the England squad who finished third at this summer’s World Cup, starting the quarter-final victory against Norway and 2-1 semi-final defeat by Argentina.
